subject: forensic-medicine
title: Mechanical injuries and medicolegal aspects of wounds

steps.tx: Mechanical injuries are classed as blunt force, sharp force or patterned injuries. Blunt force causes **abrasion**, **contusion**, **laceration** and fracture. Sharp force causes incised wounds, stab wounds and chop wounds. Knowing which group a wound belongs to is the first exam step. A lathi, for example, is blunt, so it cannot cause an incised wound. Pointed weapons cause stab wounds, where depth is the largest dimension.
steps.say: Mechanical injuries fall into blunt force, sharp force and patterned injuries. Blunt force causes abrasion, contusion, laceration and fracture. Sharp force causes incised wounds, stab wounds and chop wounds. A lathi is a blunt weapon, so it cannot cause an incised wound. Pointed weapons cause stab wounds, where depth is the largest dimension. In an incised wound, length is the largest dimension.

rows: Bleeding into tissue, no skin break

steps.tx: An **abrasion** involves only the epidermis. It is caused by friction or pressure against a rough surface. There are three types. A scratch is made by a sharp point such as a pin or thorn. A graze, also called brush or friction burn, comes from sliding skin, and is common in road accidents. A **pressure abrasion** is an imprint of an object, such as a ligature mark in hanging. Patterned abrasions reproduce the shape of the object.

steps.tx: A **contusion** is bleeding into tissue after blunt force, with the skin often intact. Its colour changes with age. Red appears on day one, blue from deoxyhaemoglobin around days two to three, and bluish black or brown from haemosiderin around days four to five. Greenish haematoidin appears around days five to six, and yellow bilirubin around days seven to ten. Colour is normal by about fourteen days. Blue colour is therefore not a sign of old bruising.
steps.say: A contusion is bleeding into tissue after blunt force. Its colour changes with age. Red appears on day one, from haemoglobin. Blue appears around days two to three, from deoxyhaemoglobin. Bluish black or brown appears around days four to five, from haemosiderin. Greenish colour from haematoidin appears around days five to six. Yellow from bilirubin appears around days seven to ten. Colour is normal by about fourteen days.

steps.tx: A **laceration** is a tear of skin or tissue caused by blunt force applied over a broad area. Edges are irregular, with tissue bridges and bruising at the margins. Hair bulbs, nerves and vessels are crushed, so bleeding is less than expected. A **split laceration** occurs where skin lies over bone with little fat, such as the scalp, eyebrow or cheekbone. It can look like an incised wound. Avulsion is tearing away of tissue by shearing force, and flaying is a large avulsion.

steps.tx: Sharp force wounds differ in shape. An **incised wound** is longer than it is deep, has clean edges, and bleeds heavily. Hesitation cuts are multiple, shallow, parallel marks beside the main wound. They are typical of suicidal attempts and are not found in homicidal assault. Wounds on the nose, ears and genitals are usually homicidal. Harakiri is a Japanese ritual suicide by abdominal stabbing, and defence wounds on the hands and forearms suggest an attempt to resist attack.

steps.tx: Medicolegal grading in India follows the Indian Penal Code. Under section 320, **grievous hurt** includes emasculation, permanent loss of sight or hearing, privation of a limb or joint, permanent facial disfigurement, and fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth. It also covers hurt that endangers life or causes twenty days of severe pain or inability to follow daily routine. Section 319 defines hurt, and simple injury heals without lasting deformity. A superficial abrasion on the face is not grievous.
